content.text:
Here is what was added and how it matches your sketch.

### What you have
- **Vite + React + TypeScript** with **D3** for the chart.
- **S&P 500** as Yahoo’s **`^GSPC`** daily closes (5 years in `scripts/fetch-gspc.mjs`).
- **No API keys**: Yahoo’s public chart URL is used **only from Node** during `npm run data` / `npm run build` / `npm run dev`. The result is written to **`public/gspc.json`**, so the deployed site is static and the browser never calls Yahoo (which avoids CORS and keys).
- **Interactive**: **brush** on the lower timeline to zoom the main series; **hover** for crosshair, dot, and tooltip with date and close.

### Commands
- **`npm run dev`** — refreshes `public/gspc.json`, then starts Vite.
- **`npm run data`** — only updates `public/gspc.json`.
- **`npm run build`** — fetches data, then builds to **`dist/`** (serve `dist` as static files).

### Main files
- `scripts/fetch-gspc.mjs` — Yahoo → `public/gspc.json`
- `src/Sp500Chart.tsx` — D3 line chart, brush, tooltip
- `src/App.tsx` — layout and copy

Yahoo can change or rate-limit this unofficial endpoint; if that happens, you still keep the last successful `public/gspc.json` in the repo so the static app keeps working until you refresh data again.

Noting `jmalicki.github.io` hosts your Hugo blog. Deploying this app as a project site at `https://jmalicki.github.io/sp500-chart/` avoids overwriting the blog. Configuring Vite base path, adding a GitHub Actions workflow, initializing git, and creating/pushing the repo.

input.contents:
name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
      - name: Install and build
        env:
          BASE_PATH: /${{ github.event.repository.name }}/
        run: npm ci && npm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

### Live site
**[https://jmalicki.github.io/sp500-chart/](https://jmalicki.github.io/sp500-chart/)** (returns 200; deploy finished successfully.)

### Repo
**[https://github.com/jmalicki/sp500-chart](https://github.com/jmalicki/sp500-chart)**

### Why it is `/sp500-chart/` and not the site root
Your user Pages repo **[jmalicki.github.io](https://github.com/jmalicki/jmalicki.github.io)** is already a **Hugo** blog. Putting this app in that repo’s root would replace the blog. This app is published as a **project** site instead, still under your **`github.io`** domain, with base path **`/sp500-chart/`**.

### What was configured
- **`vite.config.ts`**: `base` from `BASE_PATH` (set in CI to `/${{ github.event.repository.name }}/`).
- **`Sp500Chart.tsx`**: loads data with `` `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}gspc.json` `` so it works under a subpath.
- **`.github/workflows/pages.yml`**: build + `upload-pages-artifact` + `deploy-pages`.
- **GitHub Pages** for that repo was switched to **GitHub Actions** via the API.

Pushes to **`main`** rebuild and redeploy automatically. If you ever want this at **`https://jmalicki.github.io/`** instead, you’d need to merge it into the Hugo repo in a way that keeps your blog (e.g. only under a subpath from Hugo) or replace the blog on purpose.

### Narrative (for consumers)
The page is now an **end-to-end demo** with three numbered steps:

1. **Initial prompt** — The real whiteboard **PNG** (`public/original-sketch.png`), with a short explanation of what it asked for.  
2. **Build conversation** — The exported **Cursor transcript** (`public/chat-transcript.jsonl`): user/assistant turns, message text as `pre`, and each **tool call** in a **`<details>`** block so people can skim or open inputs.  
3. **Result** — The same **interactive chart** as before, plus a short note on how data and transcript get refreshed for a new demo.

### Code
- **`src/ChatTranscript.tsx`** — Loads the JSONL from `BASE_URL`, parses each line, renders the structured log.  
- **`src/App.tsx`** — Demo hero + the three sections above.  
- **`src/App.css`** — Step styling, scrollable transcript panel, tool blocks.  
- **`index.html`** — Title updated to match the demo.

### Deploy
Changes are **committed and pushed** to `jmalicki/sp500-chart`; GitHub Actions will redeploy **https://jmalicki.github.io/sp500-chart/**.

To refresh the **transcript** later (e.g. after more chat), overwrite `public/chat-transcript.jsonl` from your Cursor export and push again—the footer mentions that flow.
